supporting_points: The alternatives degrade at this size: CSS `clip-path`/`mask` polygons and `border` triangle hacks produce fractional-pixel, anti-aliased edges that look 'mushy' at 8px, offer no clean half-fill or thin ring, and are hard to keep hairline-subtle; unicode glyphs (▲■◆●◐) vary by platform font, baseline, and metrics, so they render inconsistently and blurry.

It uses only `var(--status-wip)` — the fill and the outline share the same token — satisfying the no-second-color constraint while automatically respecting the existing light/dark theme values (#a371f7 / #8250df) already defined in styles.css.

It slots into the current architecture with minimal change: the dot is already an 8px `border-radius:50%` span colored via `background-color: var(${colorVar})`; add a `.status-dot--wip` variant that swaps the flat background for the gradient + border, keyed off the existing `wip` status/`--status-wip` colorVar mapping in status.ts, so no markup, SVG asset, or data-model change is required.

Because `--status-neutral` is already themed per mode (#6e7681 dark / #818b98 light) and transparency simply shows the underlying `--canvas-*` background, the same rule works correctly on both light and dark backgrounds with no mode-specific center fill needed.

Rendering shapes with CSS `clip-path`/`mask-image` on `.status-dot` (instead of inline SVG or an inline background) means the element's `background-color` is what fills the shape, so the existing inline `backgroundColor: var(${colorVar})` on both markers keeps working unchanged and no higher-specificity inline rule needs to be overridden.
